pk-2955.st: WI DNR fire tower list: Frederic fire lookout (T36N R17W sec. 01), status scheduled for removal. Towers like this went up in the 1930s, many built by CCC crews, with a towerman's cabin and garage nearby. Check the footings and cabin site, and who owns the land. Single source: unconfirmed.

ls-davis-hill.st: A second state record: the WGNHS silver page reports a Keweenawan conglomerate sampled in sec. 11, T44N R6W, north of Namekagon Lake, assaying 0.36 to 1.74 troy ounces of silver per ton (Dutton, 1972); whether it is native silver is not known. This is the ground of the Chief Namakagon legend: an Ojibwe man who lived at Lake Namakagon until 1886 and, by Ashland Daily Press stories retold later, traded silver in Ashland and never showed where he got it. Charles Brown's 1930 Indian trails map runs a trail from the north end of Lake Namakagon north-east past this section and on to Ashland.
ls-davis-hill.t: National forest land (Chequamegon): detecting the open ground is allowed, but not at old camps or Native sites; ask the Washburn ranger district before taking rock samples. Follow the 1930 trail line north-east toward sec. 14 T45N R5W, where four homesteaders (Moe, Mattison, Smith, Larson) took up land in 1888-1893.
src: Charles E. Brown, Wisconsin Indian Trails Map, 1930 (WHS W014AUB)
